items.stem: In which COBOL division are record layouts and variables described?

options.rationale: Correct: the DATA DIVISION defines files and working storage, including record layouts.
The PROCEDURE DIVISION holds executable logic, not data definitions.
That division names the program and its author.
That division maps files to the system, not record layouts.

items.stem: Which statements about the COBOL PICTURE clause are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: PIC 9(5) describes a five-digit numeric field
options.rationale: Correct: 9 denotes a digit position and (5) repeats it five times.

options.text: Edited pictures like PIC $$,$$9.99 are for display formatting
options.rationale: Correct: edited clauses insert symbols for presentation, not computation.

options.text: PIC X fields are used for arithmetic
options.rationale: X denotes alphanumeric data, which is not used directly in arithmetic.

options.text: A PICTURE clause sets the paragraph execution order
options.rationale: PICTURE describes data; it has nothing to do with control flow.

items.explanation: Correct: 9 denotes a digit position and (5) repeats it five times.; Correct: edited clauses insert symbols for presentation, not computation.

items.stem: Why should a COBOL program check FILE STATUS after file operations?

options.text: To detect and handle I/O conditions such as end-of-file or a failed open
options.rationale: Correct: the status code reports success or specific error conditions so the program can react.
It reports outcomes; it does not change performance.
Sorting is a separate operation, unrelated to file status.
Working storage is defined in the DATA DIVISION, not via file status.
